_comment: Contingency Plan generator. Authored at the Phase 2 assessability floor; pairs naturally with the CM plan's backup_strategy group and the IR plan's recovery phase. Note the meta-quirk: CP-2 (Contingency Plan) is satisfied BY this very document.
title: Contingency Plan
description: Documents how the system continues to operate during a disruption and how it recovers afterwards. Covers the controls of the CP family in NIST SP 800-53 r5 and aligns with NIST SP 800-34 r1 (Contingency Planning Guide for Federal Information Systems).
intro_template:
This Contingency Plan documents the contingency-planning approach for {system_name}. It establishes the recovery objectives, alternate sites, backup strategy, telecommunications continuity, training, exercises, and safe-mode operations needed to maintain or restore mission-critical functions during a disruption.

The scope covers the Business Impact Analysis (BIA) underpinning the recovery objectives, the alternate storage and processing strategy, system backup and recovery procedures, telecommunications continuity, training and exercises, and degraded-operation modes within the {system_name} authorization boundary. The plan is consistent with NIST SP 800-53 r5 (Contingency Planning family) and NIST SP 800-34 r1 (Contingency Planning Guide for Federal Information Systems).

This document satisfies the CP-2 control requirement for the system to maintain a documented contingency plan.
approach_template: Contingency planning for {system_name} is owned by {cp_program_lead}. The Business Impact Analysis (§4.2) establishes a Recovery Time Objective of {rto_target} and a Recovery Point Objective of {rpo_target}. Alternate storage and processing arrangements are described in §4.3. System backups are taken per the strategy in §4.4 and recovery executes per the runbooks in §4.5. Telecommunications continuity, training and exercise programs, and safe-mode operations are documented in the sub-sections below.
continuous_monitoring_template: Contingency-planning effectiveness for {system_name} is tracked through the metrics in §6.1 (RTO / RPO performance during exercises and real events, exercise findings closed within target, backup-success rate, restoration-test outcomes). The plan itself is reviewed at the cadence in §6.2; lessons learned from exercises and real disruptions trigger interim revisions.
integration_template: This Contingency Plan does not stand alone. The IR family coordinates recovery actions during cybersecurity incidents; the CM family supplies the baseline configurations from which systems are restored; the SI family provides system-monitoring infrastructure that detects degraded operation. The following cross-references identify the specific artifacts and locations where CP-related content is exchanged with other RMF deliverables.

family_questions.label: Approach basics
family_questions.description: Program ownership and the recovery objectives that drive everything else.

questions.label: Contingency-planning program lead
questions.help: Role accountable for keeping the plan current and the program operating (e.g., 'Director of IT Operations', 'Business Continuity Manager').

questions.label: Recovery Time Objective (RTO)
questions.help: Target time from disruption to restored operation (e.g., '4 hours', '1 business day'). Drives the alternate-site and backup strategies.

questions.label: Recovery Point Objective (RPO)
questions.help: Maximum acceptable data loss measured in time (e.g., '1 hour', '24 hours'). Drives the backup frequency.

questions.label: Maximum Tolerable Period of Disruption (MTPD / MTD)
questions.help: Hard upper bound on how long the system can be down before consequences become unacceptable. Drives the alternate-processing strategy.

questions.label: Mission criticality tier
questions.help: How critical the system is to the mission. Federal MEF/PMEF terminology per FCD 1; lower tiers are organizational classifications.

family_questions.label: Business Impact Analysis (BIA)
family_questions.description: What functions the system supports, what depends on it, and the tolerance for disruption.

questions.label: Critical functions supported
questions.help: Mission / business functions the system supports. State which are time-critical and why.

questions.label: Upstream dependencies
questions.help: Other systems / services this system depends on (auth, network, storage, payments, etc.). Recovery cannot complete without these. Reference SA-9 if external.

questions.label: Downstream dependents
questions.help: Systems / services that depend on THIS system. They will also be affected by a disruption.

questions.label: BIA owner role
questions.help: Role responsible for keeping the BIA current. Often the System Owner or Business Continuity Manager.

family_questions.label: Alternate Storage and Processing
family_questions.description: Off-site storage and failover processing capabilities (CP-6, CP-7).

questions.label: Alternate storage site
questions.help: Where backups and configuration baselines live in off-site / cross-region storage. Distance from primary, access controls.

questions.label: Alternate processing site
questions.help: Where the system can run when the primary is unavailable. Cloud cross-region, hot/warm/cold site, mutual-aid agreement.

questions.label: Alternate-site readiness
options: Warm site (provisioned but not running; minutes-to-hours RTO)

questions.label: Geographic separation
questions.help: Distance from primary site in miles / km, or cloud-region pair (e.g., 'us-gov-west-1 → us-gov-east-1, ~2400 mi').

questions.label: Site activation / access procedure
questions.help: How the alternate site is activated. Who authorizes? What credentials / access are pre-positioned?

family_questions.label: System Backup Strategy
family_questions.description: Backup types, frequency, retention, and integrity verification (CP-9). Overlaps with the CM plan's backup_strategy group; the CP plan focuses on disaster-recovery use, the CM plan focuses on configuration restoration.

questions.label: Backup frequency
questions.help: How often each backup type runs. Tied to RPO target.

questions.label: Backup retention
questions.help: How long each backup type is retained. Often shorter for incremental, longer for full.

questions.label: Offsite copy
questions.help: Where the offsite copy lives. Same as alternate storage site or distinct? Encryption in transit and at rest.

questions.label: Integrity verification cadence
questions.help: How often backup integrity is verified (hash check + restore test). Separate from full restoration test.

questions.label: Restoration test cadence
questions.help: How often a real restore is exercised end-to-end (e.g., 'Quarterly restore-from-cold to scratch environment').

family_questions.label: Recovery Strategy
family_questions.description: How the system is restored from backup or alternate site (CP-10).

questions.label: Recovery phases
questions.help: Phases per NIST SP 800-34: Activation/Notification → Recovery → Reconstitution → Plan Deactivation. Document who does what at each phase.

questions.label: Recovery runbook location
questions.help: Where the technical step-by-step runbook lives. Should be accessible during a primary-site outage.

questions.label: Recovery decision authority
questions.help: Role authorized to declare a contingency event and trigger recovery (e.g., 'CP Program Lead in coordination with System Owner').

questions.label: Component recovery priority order
questions.help: Order in which components / services are restored. Database first? Auth first? Document the dependency chain.

questions.label: Reconstitution validation
questions.help: How the recovered system is validated before returning to production (smoke tests, security scans, data-integrity checks).

questions.label: Primary telecommunications service
questions.help: Main connectivity for the system (carrier + technology, e.g., 'AT&T MPLS + fiber').

questions.label: Alternate telecommunications service
questions.help: Diverse-path backup connectivity. Different carrier? Different technology? Different physical entry to the building?

questions.label: Diversity verification cadence
questions.help: How often path diversity is verified — carriers can converge to common physical paths over time without notice.

family_questions.label: Training and Exercises (CP-3, CP-4)
family_questions.description: Contingency-specific training and the exercise program.

questions.label: CP training audiences
options: All system users (general awareness of safe-mode)

questions.label: CP training cadence
options: Quarterly tabletop bites + annual full training

questions.label: Exercise types performed
options: Full-scale (failover to alternate site, real systems)

questions.label: After-action / lessons-learned process
questions.help: How exercise findings are tracked to closure (POA&M, internal tracker), and the cadence for revalidating closure.

family_questions.label: Safe Mode and Degraded Operations (CP-12)
family_questions.description: How the system continues operating in a degraded state during a disruption.

questions.label: Safe-mode definition
questions.help: What functions remain available in safe mode? What's disabled? Read-only access only? Reduced user populations?

questions.label: Safe-mode entry triggers
questions.help: What conditions cause the system to enter safe mode (automated or manual). Detection thresholds.

questions.label: User communication during degradation
questions.help: How users are informed of degraded operation and remaining capabilities (status page, banner, email).

questions.label: Safe-mode exit criteria
questions.help: Conditions for returning to full operation. Validation steps before exit.

family_questions.label: System Criticality Overview
family_questions.description: High-level summary of how critical the system is to the mission.

questions.label: Approximate users affected by disruption
questions.help: Order-of-magnitude count of users / dependent systems who would be impacted.

questions.label: Revenue / mission impact per hour of disruption
questions.help: If quantifiable. Otherwise qualitative — 'mission-essential', 'core operations halted', etc.

questions.label: Compliance impact of disruption
questions.help: Regulatory / contractual obligations that disruption would violate (uptime SLA, public-facing service requirement, etc.).

family_questions.label: Contingency Metrics & KPIs
family_questions.description: Metrics tracked to demonstrate CP control effectiveness over time.

questions.label: Tracked metrics
suggestions: RTO actual vs target (median + worst case)
RPO actual vs target (median + worst case)
Mean time to declare contingency event
% recovery runbooks current within review cadence

family_questions.label: Plan Review Cadence
family_questions.description: When and why the plan is revised.

questions.label: Triggers beyond scheduled review
questions.help: Events that force a plan revision outside the annual schedule (real disruption, organizational restructure, major architecture change).

questions.label: Plan distribution / access control
questions.help: Who receives the plan, and how access is controlled (the plan often contains procedural detail useful to attackers — control distribution accordingly).

family_questions.label: Cross-references to other RMF artifacts
family_questions.description: Where this plan plugs into the broader RMF package.

questions.label: SSP section reference
questions.help: Where in the SSP the CP control implementations are summarized (e.g., 'SSP §13.7').

questions.label: POA&M ID prefix for CP findings
questions.help: Convention for CP-related POA&M items (e.g., 'POAM-CP-').

questions.label: IR plan cross-reference
questions.help: How recovery from cybersecurity incidents coordinates with the IR plan's recovery phase.

questions.label: CM plan backup_strategy cross-reference
questions.help: How CP backup activities coordinate with the CM plan's baseline-storage and integrity-protection approach.

questions.label: CA-7 continuous-monitoring strategy reference
questions.help: Pointer to the CA-7 monitoring strategy document tying CP continuous-monitoring metrics to the broader ConMon plan.

prompts: **This document satisfies CP-2.** State that explicitly in the implementation narrative.
Reference the document version / approval signatures.
Identify the BIA — see §4.2.
Address coordination with related plans (IR — recovery; OEP — Occupant Emergency; COOP — Continuity of Operations).
Document the review cadence — see §6.2.
Reference CP-2(1) coordination with related plans, CP-2(3) resume essential mission/business functions, CP-2(8) identify critical assets.
evidence_suggestions: Plan-approval record (System Owner / ISSO / AO signatures)

extra_fields.label: Plan owner role
extra_fields.help: Role responsible for keeping the plan current (typically CP Program Lead, often the BCM).

extra_fields.label: Critical assets identified
extra_fields.help: Summary of the critical assets identified per CP-2(8). Detail typically lives in the BIA.

prompts: Reference §4.7 — training audiences and cadence.
Document the role-based training content.
Address training records and how completion is tracked.
Reference CP-3(1) simulated events for incorporating training in operational realism.

extra_fields.label: Training-records system of record
extra_fields.help: LMS or other system tracking individual completion.

extra_fields.label: Use of simulated events in training
options: Yes — every CP training cycle includes simulated event exercise
Yes — quarterly drills supplement classroom training
Yes — annual exercise serves as simulated event

prompts: Reference §4.7 — exercise types and cadence.
Document specific scenarios exercised (regional outage, ransomware, primary-site loss, etc.).
Address coordination with related-plan exercises (IR + CP joint exercise).
Document how findings are tracked to closure.
Reference CP-4(1) coordinated with related plans, CP-4(2) alternate processing site, CP-4(4) full recovery and reconstitution.

extra_fields.label: Full recovery & reconstitution tested?
options: Yes — last full reconstitution test within review cadence
Partial — components tested separately, not end-to-end
extra_fields.help: CP-4(4) requires full recovery + reconstitution exercise. Document where you stand.

extra_fields.label: Joint IR/CP exercise cadence
extra_fields.help: How often IR and CP teams exercise together on a scenario that crosses both domains.

prompts: Identify the alternate storage site — see §4.3.
Document the geographic separation and distance from primary.
Address access controls and physical / logical security at the alternate site.
Reference CP-6(1) separation from primary site, CP-6(2) recovery time / point objectives, CP-6(3) accessibility.
evidence_suggestions: Disaster scenario analysis showing alternate site is unaffected by same disruption

extra_fields.label: Alternate storage provider
extra_fields.help: Cloud region pair, third-party vault service, or in-house remote facility.

extra_fields.label: Access during emergency
extra_fields.help: How storage is accessed when the primary site is down. Pre-positioned credentials, network-path independence.

prompts: Identify the alternate processing site — see §4.3.
State the readiness tier (hot / warm / cold / mutual aid).
Document the failover process and decision authority.
Address the time required to bring up operations at the alternate site (relate to RTO).
Reference CP-7(1) separation from primary, CP-7(2) accessibility, CP-7(3) priority of service, CP-7(4) preparation for use.

extra_fields.label: Priority of service guarantee
extra_fields.help: Per CP-7(3) — contractual priority for restoration when the alternate site is shared with other tenants.

prompts: Reference §4.6 — primary and alternate telecommunications services.
State the carriers used and the diversity model (different carrier, different technology, different physical entry).
Document TSP enrollment for federal-priority restoration if applicable.
Reference CP-8(1) priority of service provisions, CP-8(2) single points of failure, CP-8(3) separation of providers, CP-8(4) provider contingency plans.

extra_fields.label: Last carrier-diversity verification
extra_fields.help: Date of last verification that primary and alternate paths are physically and operationally distinct.

extra_fields.label: Provider contingency-plan attestations
extra_fields.help: Summary of CP-8(4) — what each carrier has attested to about their own contingency posture.

prompts: Reference §4.4 — backup types, frequency, retention.
Document integrity verification + restoration testing — see §4.4.
Address backup encryption (at rest + in transit).

Reference CP-9(1) testing of backup information, CP-9(2) test restoration using sampling, CP-9(3) separate storage for critical information, CP-9(5) transfer to alternate storage site, CP-9(8) cryptographic protection.

extra_fields.label: Critical information stored separately?
options: Yes — separate logical storage and access boundary
No — same infrastructure as full backups
extra_fields.help: CP-9(3) requires critical info (e.g., critical control parameters) to be backed up separately from general system backups.

extra_fields.label: Cryptographic protection of backups
extra_fields.help: Encryption at rest + in transit. Key management. Reference SC-13 / SC-28 alignment.

prompts: Reference §4.5 — recovery phases and runbooks.
State the RTO target and document actual recovery times from exercises.
Address protection of the recovery process itself (recovery operators with elevated access; tamper protection of recovery media).
Reference CP-10(2) transaction recovery, CP-10(4) restore within time period, CP-10(6) component protection during recovery.
evidence_suggestions: Recovery-time data over last several exercises

extra_fields.label: Transaction recovery approach (CP-10(2))
extra_fields.help: For transactional systems — how in-flight transactions are handled across recovery. Roll-forward from logs, two-phase commit recovery, etc.

extra_fields.label: Protection of recovery process
extra_fields.help: How the recovery process itself is protected (recovery accounts with elevated privileges; tamper-evidence on recovery media; verification of recovered system before reconnection).

glossary.definition: Architecture where multiple instances simultaneously serve traffic across geographic regions. Failure of one region triggers automatic re-routing without manual recovery.
Architecture where a primary instance serves traffic and a standby instance takes over on failure. Failover is faster than warm-site activation but requires explicit switchover.
Document produced after an exercise or real disruption summarizing what happened, what worked, what didn't, and corrective actions.
Facility (physical or cloud) prepared to take over operation when the primary site is unavailable. Tier (hot / warm / cold) drives RTO.
Off-site location holding copies of backup data and configuration baselines, geographically separated from the primary site.
An organization-wide plan covering continuity of business functions during a disruption. Encompasses but is broader than the Contingency Plan / DRP.
Analysis identifying mission-critical functions, their dependencies, and the impact of disruption. Drives RTO / RPO targets.
An alternate site providing only the basic capability (space, power, telecom). Equipment and data must be brought in. Days-level RTO.
Federal continuity-planning concept covering an organization's ability to continue Mission Essential Functions during a disruption. Per FCD 1.
A focused plan covering technology recovery — restoring IT systems and data after a disruption. The CP is closely related but broader.
The process of switching operations from a failed component or site to a backup. Can be automatic or manual.
An alternate site with continuously running, fully provisioned infrastructure that mirrors the primary site. Near-zero RTO.

glossary.term: Maximum Tolerable Period of Disruption (MTPD / MTD)
glossary.definition: Hard upper bound on system downtime before consequences become unacceptable. RTO must be less than MTPD.
Per FCD 1, a function an organization must perform to support its statutory mission. Cannot be deferred during a continuity event.
Reciprocal arrangement between organizations to provide assistance to each other during a contingency event. Typically formalized in an MOU.
An MEF that supports the performance of a federal department's National Essential Function (NEF). Highest-tier criticality.
The maximum acceptable amount of data loss measured in time. Drives backup frequency. Example: RPO of 1 hour requires backups at least hourly.
The target time to restore a system after disruption. Drives the alternate-site readiness tier and recovery procedures.
The phase after recovery in which the system is fully restored to operational state, validated, and reconnected to dependent services.
A degraded operational mode that maintains a subset of system functions during a disruption. Typically excludes high-risk operations.
A component whose failure would cause loss of system availability. CP design seeks to eliminate or minimize SPOFs.
A federal program that authorizes priority installation and restoration of National Security and Emergency Preparedness telecommunications services.
An alternate site with provisioned infrastructure that is not actively running. Activation takes minutes to hours; RTO is typically several hours.
